# Aletheia Aegis: Runtime Enforcement for Autonomous Agent Outputs > A deterministic, sub-millisecond guard for model outputs. Fail-closed on irreversible harm, fast enough to sit on every response, with an optional semantic judge for the cases patterns cannot settle. Aegis is the output plane of the Aletheia safety framework. It inspects generated text before it reaches a user, blocks credential leaks and life-safety failures outright, and flags everything else for audit or disclaimer. It runs offline by default, on CPU, with no response text retained. Version 0.3.0. Apache 2.0. TypeScript, Node.js 18/20/22. ## Why Aegis exists Built for platform, security, and AI infrastructure teams deploying tool-using agents into regulated or high-throughput production environments. Production agents need safety that does not break the product. The common approach, running a second LLM as judge on 100 percent of outbound traffic, fails on three counts at scale: - Latency. A 1,000 to 4,000 ms penalty per turn breaks streaming and multi-step agentic loops. - Cost. A secondary frontier model on every payload turns safety into a cost center, roughly $0.002 to $0.02 per evaluation, tens of thousands of dollars monthly at scale. - Reliability. A probabilistic model policing another probabilistic model inherits prompt injection, evaluator hallucination, and nondeterministic bypasses. Aegis takes the opposite starting point: enforce the non-negotiable invariants deterministically, at wire speed, and reserve model judgment for the small set of cases where semantics actually matter. That is the core design bet. Deterministic first, semantic second, fail-closed throughout. ## Principles - Deterministic first. Pattern and structural checks run on every output. No network call, no model call, no variance. - Fail-closed on irreversible harm. Credential exfiltration and life-safety violations block immediately. They are never sent to an external judge and cannot be overruled by one. - Semantic judgment is optional and pre-redacted. When enabled, a judge sees only masked payloads, under strict rubrics, with injection defenses on the review path itself. - Zero retention by default. Telemetry stores verdict counts, signature IDs, and timings only. No prompt or response text in logs. - Honest boundaries. Aegis is a fast first-line filter, not a proof of completeness. Its limits are documented below, not buried. ## Architecture flowchart TB subgraph Host["Host application / Agent runtime"] A[Raw model response stream] end subgraph Aegis["Aletheia Aegis: Runtime Safety Platform"] direction TB B["Stage 1: Deterministic engine
DFA and structural checks, p95 0.019-0.029 ms
S1 Grounding, S2a Identity, S3 PII/Credentials,
S4 Context, S5 Medical/Legal, S6 Life-safety, S7 Attribution"] B --> C{ verdict? } C -- "BLOCK: S3 credentials, S6 harm" --> D["Hard block
Immediate fail-closed termination
No judge dispatch, no exfiltration risk"] C -- "ALLOW / FLAG" --> E["Optional Stage 2: Semantic judge
Pre-redacted, anti-injection
S6 can never be overruled"] E --> F["Citation check
Crossref: DOI, arXiv, PMID"] F --> G["Audit telemetry
Metadata and timing counts only"] end A --> B D --> H[Blocked: no output delivered] G --> I[Governed response to user] ### How the two stages work Stage 1: Deterministic edge engine. Every output is evaluated on CPU in 0.019 to 0.029 ms at p95. Irreversible failures trigger an immediate hard block. The upstream judge is skipped entirely, which saves cost and removes the exfiltration path. Stage 2: Optional semantic judge. For subjective or complex epistemic checks, an external judge (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini) can be called under strict rubrics. Detected secrets are masked before dispatch, life-safety findings can never be overruled, and heuristic defenses catch reviewer-targeted prompt injections. ## Where Aegis fits: the Aletheia dual layer Aletheia standardizes nine failure signatures across the agentic lifecycle, grounded in 2,571 real-world incident records from the AI Incident Database, AVID, and the MIT AI Risk Repository. Aegis covers the output plane. Its companion, aletheia-mcp, covers the action plane. S3 is split by plane by design, so no single layer is a single point of failure: - Action plane (aletheia-mcp): guards tool execution (shell commands, filesystem mutations, database writes, SSRF calls) before execution. - Output plane (Aegis): guards generated token streams (SSNs, API keys, credentials, private keys, Luhn-valid cards) before presentation. ## What it enforces ## Performance and evaluation Benchmarked on Linux x86_64 and Apple Silicon, Node.js 18/20/22, single core unless noted. Held-out evaluation used 575 real model outputs across 30+ open and frontier models. Batches 10-11 replay offline with no external API cost: npm run eval:heldout:judge Labels were committed before measurement. The 90.2 percent figure is the balanced-policy result with the semantic judge enabled; patterns alone catch less, which is why the two-stage design exists. See eval/ for the labeled cases and replay instructions. ### Adversarial testing Six rounds of cross-family adversarial testing, conducted with Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Gemini 3.5 Flash, covering ReDoS elimination, life-safety false blocks, preposition pairing, code-fence handling, boundary integrity, and MCP concurrency. Each round is documented in docs/audits/ ; the test suite reproduces the checks offline. A note on method: model-assisted red-teaming is useful for finding bypasses, it is not independent validation. The held-out numbers above are the empirical claim. The adversarial rounds are the hardening process behind them. ## Security: zero retention - No response text in audit trails. Telemetry and metrics store verdict counters, signature IDs, and timings only. - Pre-judge secret masking. If a judge is enabled, detected credentials, API keys, and SSNs are masked before dispatch to any external provider. - Fail-closed isolation. Pattern-based blocks halt immediately and are never sent to external judges. - Verified by leak tests. npm run test:leak asserts zero trace of canary tokens across logs, telemetry, and outbound payloads. ## Quick start ### 1. CLI # Prescriptive medical directive (S5) npx aletheia-aegis --check " Take 500mg of ciprofloxacin twice daily for 10 days. " # FLAG [S5_DOSAGE_WITHOUT_DEFERRAL] # Credential leak (S3) npx aletheia-aegis --check " Database connection: postgres://admin:secretKey987654@db.prod:5432/main " # BLOCK [S3_CREDENTIAL_PAIR] (masked evidence) ### 2. MCP server (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Cline, OpenRouter) { "mcpServers" : { "aletheia-aegis" : { "command" : " npx " , "args" : [ " -y " , " aletheia-aegis " ] } } } With an optional Tier-2 judge: { "mcpServers" : { "aletheia-aegis" : { "command" : " npx " , "args" : [ " -y " , " aletheia-aegis " ], "env" : { "AEGIS_JUDGE_PROVIDER" : " anthropic " , "AEGIS_JUDGE_API_KEY" : " sk-ant-... " , "AEGIS_JUDGE_POLICY" : " balanced " , "AEGIS_VERIFY_CITATIONS" : " crossref " } } } } ### 3. TypeScript SDK Embed inside inference gateways, proxy routers, or API middleware: import { evaluateOutput } from "aletheia-aegis" ; const assessment = evaluateOutput ( { response : generatedTokens , userPrompt : userQuery , locale : "US" } ) ; if ( assessment . verdict === "BLOCK" ) { metrics . increment ( "safety.hard_block" , { signature : assessment . findings [ 0 ] . signature } ) ; throw new SecurityPolicyException ( "Generation blocked: " + assessment . explanation ) ; } if ( assessment . verdict === "FLAG" ) { auditPipeline . logEvent ( { findings : assessment . findings , latencyMs : assessment . latencyMs } ) ; } ## MCP tools Six tools, four resources, one prompt template. Resources: aegis://signatures/all , aegis://telemetry/summary , aegis://telemetry/audit-log , aegis://eval/last-scorecard . Prompt: aegis_output_review , which guides a model to remediate flagged outputs. ## Configuration ## Boundaries and threat model Transparency on limits is part of the design: - Deterministic pre-filter, not a semantic parser. Novel or deliberately obfuscated paraphrases can evade pattern heuristics. Aegis catches the common and severe classes at microsecond cost, so downstream systems can focus on edge cases. - Prose credential screening (S3). To avoid false alarms on ordinary conversation, credential checks require non-word or complex token characteristics. Single dictionary words ("your password is password") deliberately pass. Cards require valid brand prefixes and Luhn checks. Bank accounts require banking context, so utility bills and gym numbers are not blocked. - Life safety (S6). Strict verb-preposition pairing keeps benign de-escalation ("sit on the platform bench while you wait") passing with supportive resources, while lethal placements ("sit on the train tracks") block. English-first, with core French, German, and Spanish intent statements. - Citation scope (S1). Crossref verifies scholarly works (DOI, arXiv, PMID). Legal case citations retain their S1 warning by design; court registries are outside Crossref. - Single-turn scope (S8). Aegis operates on individual prompt-response pairs. Multi-turn erosion requires session-level auditing, which is the planned session auditor (see Roadmap). ## Status and roadmap Current: v0.3.0. Public release. Deterministic engine, optional judge, Crossref verification, MCP server, and SDK are stable. S4 remains experimental. Next: - Session auditor for S8 multi-turn erosion - Expanded non-English coverage for S6 - Broader held-out eval sets, with sampling methodology documented in repo - Registry listing following npm publication Contributions and issue reports are welcome. Please include a redacted reproduction case for any bypass report, never a live credential. ## Tests Everything runs offline: npm install npm run build # Compile TypeScript (tsc) npm test # Core unit checks + eval assertions (45 checks) npm run test:judge # Model judge, security, ReDoS tests (121 checks) npm run test:mcp # MCP stdio smoke test (13 checks) npm run test:mcp:adversarial # MCP stdio protocol fuzzing and sandboxing (11 checks) npm run test:stress # Concurrency and re-entrancy stress (120 tasks) npm run test:leak # Zero-leak PII/secret verification npm run test:fp # False-positive sweep on benign discourse (90 cases) npm run eval # Full 215-case benchmark (100 percent pass) npm run eval:redteam # Adversarial paraphrase suite (90.9 percent catch) npm run eval:heldout:judge # Offline replay of held-out batches 10-11 npm run benchmark # 10,000-iteration latency benchmark ## Author and citation Aletheia Aegis is authored by Vikas Shivpuriya as part of the Aletheia AI Safety Research Core. @software { shivpuriya2026aegis , author = { Vikas Shivpuriya } , title = { Aletheia Aegis: Runtime Enforcement for Autonomous Agent Outputs } , year = { 2026 } , publisher = { GitHub } , version = { 0.3.0 } , url = { https://github.com/vikasny30/aletheia-aegis } } ## License Copyright 2026 Vikas Shivpuriya. # 🌗 ShadowDiff

### Dual-Traffic Shadow Testing Engine for AI-Refactored Legacy Code

> Eliminating the 5% risk that stops enterprise CTOs from deploying AI-modernized backends to production. 🌐 Interactive Live Cloud Sandbox : https://shadowdiff-demo.fly.dev (Self-driving dual-traffic simulator active)

## 🎬 Live Terminal Walkthrough ( vhs )

## ⚡ The Problem

Enterprises are actively modernizing mission-critical legacy backends (Java 7/8 Spring monoliths, Python 2 Django, PHP 5.6 backends) into modern cloud-native services (Go, TypeScript/Node, FastAPI) using AI code migration engines.

While AI generates ~95% of refactored code accurately, the remaining 5% of hidden edge cases make production deployment an unacceptable risk :

- Subtle Serialization Discrepancies : Jackson omitting empty lists vs Go serializing null , datetime timezone truncations, float precision drift.

- Implicit Framework Quirks : Legacy servlet filter quirks, undocumented fallback headers, HTTP 200 responses with embedded error payloads.

- Database State Regressions : Silent differences in database transaction boundaries, missing audit writes, or N+1 query loop explosions.

## 💡 The Solution: ShadowDiff

ShadowDiff is a high-performance network proxy and analysis engine that duplicates real staging or production HTTP traffic, sending identical payloads to both the legacy service and the AI-refactored service simultaneously.

[ Live Inbound Traffic ] │ ▼ ┌─────────────────────────────┐ │ Envoy Gateway / Mesh │ │ (request_mirror_policies) │ └──────────────┬──────────────┘ │ ┌───────────────────┴───────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ┌───────────────────┐ ┌───────────────────┐ │ Legacy Service │ │ ShadowDiff Core │ │ (Target) │ │ (Analysis Engine)│ └─────────┬─────────┘ └─────────┬─────────┘ │ │ │ (Live Response to Client) ▼ │ ┌───────────────────┐ │ │ AI-Refactored │ │ │ Candidate (S) │ │ └─────────┬─────────┘ │ │ └───────────────────┬───────────────────┘ ▼ ┌─────────────────────────────┐ │ 3-Way Diff & SQL Comparator │ │ - P1 ⊕ P2 Noise Filter │ │ - SQL Mutation Interceptor │ │ - N+1 Query Loop Detector │ └──────────────┬──────────────┘ │ (Pure Regressions Isolated) ▼ ┌─────────────────────────────┐ │ Automated AI Test Generator │ │ - Powered by Google Gemini │ │ - Synthesizes Go/Jest Tests │ │ - Root Cause Code Fixes │ └─────────────────────────────┘

## 🚀 Key Architectural Capabilities

### 1. ⚡ Network-Level Envoy Traffic Mirroring

ShadowDiff integrates directly with Envoy Proxy and Istio Service Mesh using request_mirror_policies . Traffic is cloned asynchronously at line rate in the network layer with zero application latency penalty .

### 2. 🎯 3-Way Differential Noise Cancellation (Diffy Model)

Automatically filters out non-deterministic runtime noise (timestamps, UUIDs, session nonces) by evaluating twin baseline instances: $$\mathcal{N} = P_1 \oplus P_2$$ $$\mathcal{D} = (P_1 \oplus S) \setminus \mathcal{N}$$ Only verified contract regressions reach developer triage.

### 3. 💾 Database Mutation & SQL Side-Effect Diffing

Captures and correlates SQL statements executed by both services for each HTTP trace:

- Missing Writes : Flags when legacy wrote to audit_logs or ledger tables that modern code omitted.

- Transaction Leaks : Warns if legacy used BEGIN...COMMIT and modern ran autocommit statements.

- N+1 Query Explosions : Detects when modern ORMs loop and execute $\ge 3\times$ more queries than legacy.

### 4. 🤖 Google Gemini Regression Test Synthesis

Every isolated edge case is analyzed by Google Gemini ( gemini-2.0-flash ), which writes a turnkey integration test (Go httptest or Vitest) and diagnoses the code fix.

### 5. 🐙 Autonomous Closed-Loop GitHub PR Bot

Eliminates manual triaging by directly integrating with the GitHub API:

- Automatic Branching : Spins up shadowdiff/fix-<trace_id> from the repository's default branch.

- Test File Commitment : Automatically commits the synthesized regression test directly to the repository (e.g. tests/regression/test_drift_<trace_id>.go ).

- Rich Pull Request Generation : Opens a detailed PR with side-by-side JSON diff tables, SQL mutation waterfall analysis, N+1 query warnings, and local verification commands.

- 1-Click Triage in Console : Developers can inspect the incident in the web console and click "🚀 Open GitHub PR" to immediately open the PR on GitHub.

### 6. 🚦 CI/CD "Shadow Gating" CLI ( shadowdiff gate )

A native deployment blocker that evaluates traffic quality during pre-release soak tests or integration pipelines:

- Automated Evaluation : Assesses semantic parity, database mutations, and N+1 query loops over a specified evaluation window.

- Zero False Failure : Honors Diffy noise cancellation ( $\mathcal{N} = P_1 \oplus P_2$ ), only failing on genuine regressions.

- Pipeline Integration : Returns standard exit codes ( 0 for PASS, 1 for FAIL/violation, 2 for error) with high-impact ANSI colored terminal summaries and optional JSON format.

# Evaluate quality gate in your CI/CD pipeline: shadowdiff gate \ -dashboard-url=http://localhost:8083 \ -duration=15s \ -min-parity=100.0 \ -min-requests=50 \ -max-drifts=0 \ -allow-n-plus-one=false \ -allow-db-drift=false

### 7. 🛡️ Ephemeral Copy-on-Write (CoW) Database Sandboxing

Allows safe shadow mirroring of mutating HTTP methods ( POST , PUT , DELETE , PATCH ) with zero database pollution :

- Transactional Savepoint Rollbacks : Injects boundary headers to ensure shadow writes execute within an isolated savepoint and automatically roll back.

- Ephemeral Schema Sandboxing : Dynamically creates disposable schemas per test run and drops them upon completion.

- Serverless CoW Branching : Leverages Neon / Supabase serverless branching to clone database state instantly via API for mutating candidate runs.

## 🚦 GitHub Actions CI/CD Quality Gating Workflow

Incorporate ShadowDiff directly into your automated deployment pipeline ( .github/workflows/shadowdiff.yml ):

name : Dual-Traffic Shadow Gating on : [pull_request, push] jobs : shadow-gate : runs-on : ubuntu-latest steps : - uses : actions/checkout@v4 - uses : actions/setup-go@v5 with : go-version : ' 1.22 ' - name : Build & Start Services run : | go build -o bin/shadowdiff ./cmd/shadowdiff/main.go ./bin/legacy-service -port=:8081 & ./bin/refactored-service -port=:8082 & ./bin/shadowdiff -proxy-port=:8080 -primary-url=http://localhost:8081 -shadow-url=http://localhost:8082 -sandbox-mode=rollback & sleep 2 - name : Replay Traffic run : | for i in {1..25}; do curl -s "http://localhost:8080/api/users?id=$i" > /dev/null curl -s -X POST "http://localhost:8080/api/orders" -d '{"amount":99.50}' > /dev/null done - name : Run ShadowDiff Quality Gate run : | ./bin/shadowdiff gate \ -dashboard-url=http://localhost:8083 \ -min-parity=100.0 \ -min-requests=20 \ -allow-n-plus-one=false \ -allow-db-drift=false

## 🛠️ Quickstart with Envoy & Docker Compose

Launch the complete 5-container service mesh testbed (Envoy Gateway + ShadowDiff + Legacy Target + Twin Replica + AI Candidate):

# 1. Clone the repository git clone https://github.com/vishalrajofficial/ShadowDiff.git cd ShadowDiff # 2. Launch the Envoy Service Mesh topology docker compose -f docker-compose.envoy.yml up -d

### Send Ingress Traffic Through Envoy (Port 10000):

# Send test traffic to the Envoy Gateway (mirrored to ShadowDiff automatically): curl http://localhost:10000/api/users/1 curl -X POST http://localhost:10000/api/orders

Open the telemetry dashboard at http://localhost:8083 to inspect the live 3-way diffs, SQL mutation timeline, and Gemini-generated tests!

## ☸️ Kubernetes & Istio Service Mesh Deployment

For production Kubernetes clusters running Istio or native Envoy, deploy the included EnvoyFilter to mirror traffic dynamically:

kubectl apply -f deploy/k8s/envoy-shadow-sidecar.yaml

See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md for full architectural specifications.

# Telegram AI Bot Pro

A private TypeScript Telegram assistant with text and voice conversations, photo analysis and editing, image generation, web search with sources, document questions, projects, named conversations, explicit saved memory, usage controls, streaming replies and durable background jobs. MIT licensed.

“Pro” names this repository's feature set. It does not grant a ChatGPT subscription or provider account access.

## Get started

Requirements: Node.js 26.13+ within Node 26 , npm 11, a Telegram bot token, an OpenAI project API key with billing and model access. Outgoing voice messages require FFmpeg with libopus ; the Docker image includes it. Incoming voice transcription needs no FFmpeg.

nvm use npm ci cp .env.example .env # Fill in required settings before starting. npm run dev

Required settings:

- TELEGRAM_API_KEY : token from @BotFather .

- OPENAI_API_KEY : private OpenAI project key.

- ALLOWED_TELEGRAM_USER_IDS : comma-separated numeric IDs. Only these users in private chats are processed.

Default chat model: gpt-6.1-sol . Override it with OPENAI_CHAT_MODEL using a Responses model supporting vision, document inputs, web_search and image_generation . Missing or blank values use the default.

Default image model: gpt-image-2.5-sunburst , quality high . Default outgoing speech model: gpt-realtime-2.1-mini , voice marin . Model availability must be checked against your own account. Configuration does not establish provider acceptance.

For FFmpeg on macOS, install with brew install ffmpeg ; on Debian/Ubuntu, install the ffmpeg package. Check that your build supports the libopus encoder. FFMPEG_PATH can point to a trusted executable.

npm run build npm start

## Commands

Voice replies start off . Every outgoing voice message is labelled AI-generated voice . Text answers remain available even if narration fails. Long answers are not silently truncated for speech: use /speak with a shorter passage.

Natural-language requests can invoke image generation or web search automatically. Explicit commands provide a predictable way to request them. remember: … and forget … manage saved notes without a model call. The bot never extracts long-term notes automatically from ordinary conversation.

## Photos and documents

Send a photo or original JPEG/PNG/static WebP file, with optional instructions in its caption. Continue asking questions about it. /image , /edit and /search also work in captions. Reply to an older photo or document to attach that exact source to the current request. Generated images arrive as original PNG documents.

Supported document extensions: PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, TXT, MD, CSV, JSON . Send a document with a question, or without a caption for a summary. Follow-up questions reuse retained files. PDFs and Office files are parsed by OpenAI; text documents must be UTF-8. Signatures catch obvious PDF/Office/image mismatches; complete file validity and provider parsing are checked downstream. Embedded pictures/layout in non-PDF documents are not guaranteed to be available to the model. Convert to PDF when visual layout matters.

Reference albums collect up to ten updates during a 750 ms window and share one download deadline. Items arriving later receive the usual busy response if processing has begun. Send files separately and wait for each reply when predictable batch membership matters.

Examples:

[photo] Read this sign and translate it into English. /image A realistic cat portrait in a spacesuit, square composition [reply to that image] /edit Replace the background with a beach [PDF] Summarize the obligations and point to the relevant pages. [follow-up] What does section 4 say? /search What changed in the latest Node.js release? /new Work /remember Answer concisely in English. /voice auto

## Data and limits

Production state is saved to STATE_DB_PATH (default ./data/bot.sqlite ). Text history, images, documents, conversation names, saved notes and voice preferences are private local data. Keep this file out of source control and use a persistent Docker volume. :memory: selects disposable state. Tests inject isolated stores and do not open your production database.

Saved conversation names, notes and voice settings survive restarts. Retained message history and attachments also survive restarts within TTL and capacity limits . History defaults to one hour of inactivity and 20 complete turns per conversation. Expired histories are pruned at startup and on subsequent conversation access; names and explicit notes are retained separately. /reset preserves other conversations and saved notes. /forget removes saved notes but cannot erase earlier text containing the same information; clear affected conversations too when needed.

Foreground updates are serialized per user. A background job locks its conversation; foreground work in another conversation can proceed within the global concurrency cap. /stop remains available during foreground work. Overlapping foreground updates receive a busy response. Provider failures do not commit partial turns. Successful complete-turn writes and capacity evictions are transactional in SQLite. Text and media have bounded request/history budgets. Daily quotas and configurable estimated-spend reservations apply separately; see the Pro workspace commands below. Estimates are not provider invoices or a hard billing cap.

Text, audio, attached files, saved notes and relevant history are sent to OpenAI for requested processing. Search may send generated queries to search providers. Responses use store: false ; this does not establish zero retention by OpenAI or Telegram. Requests and raw provider exceptions are not logged. The SQLite file is access-restricted but is not encrypted at rest by this application.

## Pro workspaces and controls

Daily accounting uses UTC regardless of schedule timezone. Defaults allow 100 paid operations and $10 of configured cost estimates per owner/day. Tool calls and speech have separate limits. Failures and cancelled attempts retain their reservations because provider charges may already have occurred. Configure provider-side spending controls too. /erase retains minimal current-day quota counters to prevent limit bypass.

Projects and jobs retain files independently of conversation TTL. PDF export embeds a bundled font for Latin, Greek and Cyrillic text with limited punctuation; unsupported characters produce a clear error directing you to Markdown/JSON. No cloud PDF conversion is used. See the user guide for full syntax and lifecycle rules.

## Development and tests

npm run check # types, lint, formatting, unit tests and production compilation npm run test:unit # unit tests only; npm test is equivalent npm run test:coverage # require 100% executable src lines, branches and functions

Tests live beside their implementation in __tests__ ; shared in-memory doubles live in src/__tests__/helpers.ts . Production compilation excludes every __tests__ directory. Only test files are excluded from coverage; production code has no coverage-ignore annotations.

Only unit tests are authorized and maintained. HTTP/WebSocket transports, SQLite/filesystem access, process lifecycle, FFmpeg spawning and PDF rendering use controlled doubles. Tests do not call live services, open databases, run application subprocesses, invoke FFmpeg, build Docker or render browsers. They require no API keys and incur no API charges. Node's experimental module-mocking flag is included in test scripts.

CI runs static checks, unit tests, the 100% coverage gate and a dependency advisory query ( npm audit , network metadata only). It does not install FFmpeg or build Docker. Unit coverage establishes exercised local control flow; live model access, native SQLite durability, PDF layout, audio fidelity and deployment behavior remain unqualified. npm is the sole package manager; commit lockfile changes with dependencies.

## Documentation

- User guide

- Configuration reference

- Operations, Docker, backups and live verification

- Architecture and test conventions

- Pro roadmap and acceptance

- Changelog , contributing , security , license

Official API references: web search , image generation , file inputs , Realtime audio , Telegram Bot API .

# Lynx: The open source AI workspace you can fully customize

Docs for humans - Docs for agents - Community - Roadmap - Download for macOS

## About

Lynx is a fully-customizable AI workspace designed to keep you organized and fit your work patterns.

Most of our interactions with AI today happen through walls of text that are tiring to parse through and inefficient for working. Active AI users also quickly find themselves with more threads open than they can manage.

Lynx solves this by putting interactive interfaces at the center of our interaction with agents. Workspaces in Lynx are fully-customizable UIs, connected to the services you use, and able to trigger agents using your local Claude Code or Codex.

## Features

- 100% local : Lynx runs on your device only and does not send data anywhere.

- Use your own subscriptions : Lynx makes use of Claude Code and Codex running on your machine. Switch between them as you like.

- Connect any MCP or API : Connect any service you use via MCP or API. You can also ask Lynx to help you connect anything else.

- Templates : Official and community workspace templates for you to start from and modify to your needs.

- Fully customizable workspaces : Create as many fully custom workspaces as you want and quickly switch between them.

- Point to edit : The point tool makes it easy to point out exactly what you want changed in a UI. Changes go live as soon as the agent is done editing.

- Scheduled tasks : Schedule tools and agents to run on a cron.

## Why Lynx?

As of today, Lynx is an experiment about a better way to work with AI. It's so far proven to be very useful to me and some early testers, which is why I'm releasing it publicly, but it remains an experiment. For what it's worth though, I've done over 80% of my daily work from Lynx for a couple weeks now.

There were a few reasons for building it:

- Interacting with agents through walls of text was getting tiring and inefficient

- It was hard to keep track of everything my agents were doing

- Harnesses for coding felt like the wrong shape for other types of work

- Interactive tools and artifacts proved very useful, but ended up fragmenting work even more

- It was hard to stay in the flow jumping through various tools / programs / websites

From this, I decided to explore a way of working that was more visual and interactive, while still feeling cohesive rather than fragmented.

A lot of people and companies seem to have come to the conclusion that UIs are still very relevant for humans. Many of us still prefer to click a button that says "Do X" rather than tell an agent "Do X for me". We also like graphs, tables, and colors.

For this reason we've seen artifacts take off, and also MCP-UI starting to become more relevant (basically the little visualizations inside ChatGPT chats).

But these still feel additive to a chat experience, rather than central to our interaction with AI. Most times we're still driving everything from a chat, just using these visual tools as a resource along the way.

So with Lynx, that concept was flipped on its head. Interactive UIs are at the core of the experience, and the chat is there to augment it.

## To-dos / task tracking example

A typical workflow for a lot of people includes waking up and asking Claude: "Check Jira for tasks assigned to me and tell me the important ones to focus on today". They then receive a bunch of text back, and go back and forth on it via chat until they've gathered the necessary context to work

With Lynx, you'd create a workspace called "Task Tracking" that connects to Jira and displays your list of tasks in a nice UI. Every morning an agent would look through these and prioritize for you, so that when you open the workspace you already have a clear overview of what's going on. Then, instead of going to a chat to ask about a specific task, you can add a button to trigger an agent to triage it, or even start working on it. To find the output of this agent you wouldn't need to search through dozens of threads, you just go to your Task Tracking workspace and see it from the UI.

Agentic Identity Broker manages delegation chains for on-behalf-of flows in Agentic AI, bridges distinct OAuth2 infrastructures, and provides a secure token vault. Deployed within the call path via gateways like Agentgateway , it offloads auth burdens from both agent and MCP server creators.

For users, it provides a simple way to manage consent, granting agents granular permissions across services such as Google, GitHub, Databricks, and Linear without compromising control.

## Key Features

- Secure Identity Management Agent registration, principal authentication, and session management

- OAuth2 Delegation & Consent Manage OAuth2 scopes and user consent for third-party service integrations

- Security-First Design Sensitive value redaction, command injection prevention, cryptographic validation, and fail-closed architecture

- Rich Consent Experience Modern UX for managing OAuth2 delegations with design system compliance

- Comprehensive Audit Logging Structured JSON logging for compliance and security monitoring

## Use Cases

### Internal MCP Servers

Frameworks like FastMCP can implement the whole OAuth2.1 ceremonies as mandated by the MCP spec but this means that you have to configure it for every MCP Server you deploy and maintain it. You also have to configure secure storage and basically run a multitude of OAuth2 authorization servers. With the identity broker and a gateway you can dumb down MCP server development to only provide tools on the target technology you want. OAuth2 ceremonies, token vaulting and token translation are done transparently. Because token exchange is done centrally via a gateway, this allows agents to interact with hundreds of MCP servers via one channel.

### MCP Servers for SaaS

If you want to offer an MCP server to your customers as part of your SaaS, the identity broker can provide an additional consent surface that records which agents were actually used. With centralized tool authorization, you can keep an audit trail of approvals on your side regardless of which agent the customer runs.

### Hosted Agents

The agentic identity broker can simplify agents by requiring only a single user token that can be used with an arbitrary number of MCP servers. When paired with a portal for user interactions, token procurement can be front-loaded in the portal, and the agent's responsibility is to forward this token to upstream MCP servers via a gateway.

### Delegation Chains Without User Presence

The impersonation feature allows to start delegation chains via privileged clients, like a Google Chat or Slack bridge. The broker can be instructed to trust for two independent machine identities to assume the session for a particular user. This allows to use the permissions of a user on the company chat in another third-party system.

### Central Authorization Prompts

The tool approval support in the broker allows to enforce tool calls independent of the agent interface in use. This allows a last resort check before emails get sent or documents shared with a central audit trail.

## Roadmap

Agentic Identity Broker is currently in active development. We use this project in production internally for several MCP servers and have seen good potential. We are coding in the open to gauge our approach. If you find it useful, let us know. If you'd like a feature that's missing, open an issue in our GitHub repo .

While this project was created by professionals with decades of experience in the identity space (including building multiple OIDC and OAuth2 providers), it was developed with a strong focus on agentic engineering and spec-driven development. We review every PR and prioritize sound engineering practices over convenience.

Major roadmap topics include: (a) formalizing token exchange for agent-to-agent calls, (b) intent based authorization and (c) user facing acticity logs.
